## Question 1


## Question 2

```{r}
# Step 1 Creatig a data frame as per the question 
MIDSEM_DDD$df <- tibble(  # using tibble to create a data frame 
  individual_id      = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),        
  years_of_education = c(10, 14, 12, 16, 8),           
  employment_status  = c("Employed", "Unemployed",
                         "Employed", "Employed",
                         "Unemployed"),                 
  monthly_income     = c(25000, 0, 18000, 45000, 0)     
)
print(MIDSEM_DDD$df)

# -----------------------------------------------
# Part (a): Rename variables to better names
# rename() changes column names
# new_name = old_name is the syntax
# -----------------------------------------------

MIDSEM_DDD$df <- MIDSEM_DDD$df %>%
  rename(
    edu_years      = years_of_education,   # shorter and cleaner name
    income_monthly = monthly_income        # clearer name
  )

print(MIDSEM_DDD$df)

# -----------------------------------------------
# Part (b): Create new variable - more than 12 years of education?
# mutate() adds a new column to the data frame
# ifelse(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false)
# -----------------------------------------------

MIDSEM_DDD$df <- MIDSEM_DDD$df %>%
  mutate(
    high_edu = ifelse(edu_years > 12, TRUE, FALSE)
  )
print(MIDSEM_DDD$df)


# -----------------------------------------------
# Part (c): Subset - keep only individuals with high_edu == TRUE
# filter() keeps only rows that match the condition
# -----------------------------------------------

MIDSEM_DDD$df_subset <- MIDSEM_DDD$df %>%
  filter(high_edu == TRUE)  
print(MIDSEM_DDD$df_subset)

# -----------------------------------------------
# Part (d): Keep only individual_id and high_edu columns
# select() chooses which columns to keep
# -----------------------------------------------

MIDSEM_DDD$df_final <- MIDSEM_DDD$df_subset %>%
  select(individual_id, high_edu)  
print(MIDSEM_DDD$df_final)

```

## Question 3

```{r}

# Step 1: Create data frame with 4 numeric variables
MIDSEM_DDD$df3 <- data.frame(
  a = c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60),    
  b = c(5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55),     
  c = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12),        
  d = c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11)          
)
print(MIDSEM_DDD$df3)


# -----------------------------------------------
# Part (a): Replace some elements with NA (missing values)
# [row, column] targets a specific cell in the data frame
# -----------------------------------------------

MIDSEM_DDD$df3[2, "a"] <- NA    
MIDSEM_DDD$df3[4, "b"] <- NA    
MIDSEM_DDD$df3[1, "c"] <- NA    # row 1 of column c becomes missing
MIDSEM_DDD$df3[3, "d"] <- NA    

print(MIDSEM_DDD$df3)

# -----------------------------------------------
# Part (b): Write Z-score function
# Z-score formula: (value - mean) / standard deviation
# na.rm = TRUE means ignore NA values during calculation
# -----------------------------------------------

MIDSEM_DDD$z_score <- function(x) {
  (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
} # x is the input numeric vector
  # mean(x, na.rm=TRUE) calculates average, skipping NA values (same for sd also)
 

# -----------------------------------------------
# Part (c): Apply function to transform the data frame
# mutate() creates or changes columns
# -----------------------------------------------

MIDSEM_DDD$df3_change <- MIDSEM_DDD$df3 %>%
  mutate(
    # Replace columns a, b, c with their z-scores
    across(c(a, b, c), MIDSEM_DDD$z_score),

    # New variable mean_deviation = each value of d minus the mean of d
    mean_deviation = d - mean(d, na.rm = TRUE),

    # New variable sum_z = sum of z-scores of a, b, c for each row
    # rowSums() adds values across columns row by row
    sum_z = rowSums(across(c(a, b, c)), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(MIDSEM_DDD$df3_change)


```

## Question 4

```{r}
# Step 1: Create a numeric vector 
MIDSEM_DDD$vec <- c(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42)

# Step 2: Calculate the mean of the full vector ONCE before the loop
MIDSEM_DDD$vec_mean <- mean(MIDSEM_DDD$vec)   # calculates the average

# Step 3: Write the absolute deviation function
MIDSEM_DDD$abs_dev <- function(x, mean_val) {
  sqrt((x - mean_val)^2)
}

# Step 4: Preallocate empty output vector 
# numeric(length(vec)) creates a vector of zeros, same size as vec
MIDSEM_DDD$result4 <- numeric(length(MIDSEM_DDD$vec))

# Step 5: Apply function element by element using for loop
# i goes from 1 to length of vec
for (i in 1:length(MIDSEM_DDD$vec)) {
  MIDSEM_DDD$result4[i] <- MIDSEM_DDD$abs_dev(MIDSEM_DDD$vec[i], MIDSEM_DDD$vec_mean)
}
print(MIDSEM_DDD$result4)

# -----------------------------------------------
# WITHOUT for loop - same result in one line
# -----------------------------------------------
# sqrt() of squared difference gives absolute deviation
MIDSEM_DDD$result4_no_loop <- sqrt((MIDSEM_DDD$vec - mean(MIDSEM_DDD$vec))^2)
print(MIDSEM_DDD$result4_no_loop)
```

## Question 5

```{r}

# We need two vectors for two loops
MIDSEM_DDD$outer_vec <- c(2, 4, 6)    # outer values
MIDSEM_DDD$inner_vec <- c(10, 20)     # inner values

# Nested for loop:
# For each i in (2, 4, 6), loop through all j in (10, 20)
for (i in MIDSEM_DDD$outer_vec) {     
  for (j in MIDSEM_DDD$inner_vec) {     
    print(c(i, j))                     
  }
}

```

## Question 6

```{r}

# Create data frame with 5 employees
MIDSEM_DDD$df6 <- tibble(
  id     = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
  salary = c(20000, 35000, 28000, 42000, 31000)
)

# hike = fixed amount added to every employee salary
MIDSEM_DDD$hike <- 5000

# -----------------------------------------------
# PART (a) - Create empty vector FIRST before loop
# storing length in a simple variable n
# -----------------------------------------------
n <- length(MIDSEM_DDD$df6$salary)   # n = 5
new_salary <- numeric(n)              # creates --> 0 0 0 0 0

# -----------------------------------------------
# PART (b) - For loop to calculate new salary
# -----------------------------------------------
for (i in 1:n) {
  new_salary[i] <- MIDSEM_DDD$df6$salary[i] + MIDSEM_DDD$hike
}
new_salary

# -----------------------------------------------
# PART (c) - Add new_salary as a column in df6
# -----------------------------------------------
MIDSEM_DDD$df6$new_salary <- new_salary
MIDSEM_DDD$df6

# -----------------------------------------------
# PART (d) - WITHOUT for loop
# -----------------------------------------------
MIDSEM_DDD$df6$new_salary_v2 <- MIDSEM_DDD$df6$salary + MIDSEM_DDD$hike
MIDSEM_DDD$df6
```

## Question 7

```{r}

# Step 1: Create a vector of marks for 10 students
MIDSEM_DDD$marks <- c(95, 82, 67, 55, 78, 91, 60, 45, 73, 88)

# Step 2: Preallocate empty character vector to store grades
MIDSEM_DDD$grades <- character(length(MIDSEM_DDD$marks))

# Step 3: For loop with if-else to check each student's marks
for (i in 1:length(MIDSEM_DDD$marks)) {

  if (MIDSEM_DDD$marks[i] >= 90) {   # marks >= 90 gets Grade A
    MIDSEM_DDD$grades[i] <- "Grade A"

  } else if (MIDSEM_DDD$marks[i] >= 75) { # marks >= 75 but less than 90 gets Grade B
    MIDSEM_DDD$grades[i] <- "Grade B"

  } else if (MIDSEM_DDD$marks[i] >= 60) {    # marks >= 60 but less than 75 gets Grade C
    MIDSEM_DDD$grades[i] <- "Grade C"

  } else {      # marks below 60 gets Fail
    MIDSEM_DDD$grades[i] <- "Fail"
  }
}


print(MIDSEM_DDD$grades)

# Step 5: Show marks and grades together
MIDSEM_DDD$result_q7 <- tibble(
  marks  = MIDSEM_DDD$marks,   
  grades = MIDSEM_DDD$grades    
)

print(MIDSEM_DDD$result_q7)

```
